Retrieved reporting documents the regional incident identified as the Bejís wildfire in Castellón, noting an escalation during which preliminary incident reports characterized the event as a "tormenta de fuego" (firestorm) [W1]. The retrieved text also highlights consequences involving a passenger train affected along the route during the incident [W1]. 

The retrieved documentation does not provide details on the ignition cause, specific fuel conditions, local weather variables, or precise containment dates, leaving the confirmed cause and environmental drivers unverified in the supplied text. Furthermore, without defined spatial coordinates or tool measurements, the regional incident remains a plausible candidate rather than a confirmed identity for any specific mapped ground location. Detailed perimeter boundaries and verified ignition determinations require accessing complete official investigative reports or localized satellite observations.

### Root Cause & Ignition Mechanism

The available reports **do not establish the ignition cause**. This means the cause is unverified in the evidence retrieved here; it does not establish that authorities have never determined it. [5]

### Temporal Progression & Episode Duration

The automatically discovered thermal episode runs from **2012-06-30** to **2012-06-30**: **1 consecutive days** above the activity threshold. Peak: **2012-06-30**, **118,028.419 MJ/km²/day** (98,027.503 GJ). Integrated episode FRE: **98,027.503 GJ**. [6]

Threshold: 5,901.421 MJ/km²/day; background sample: 4 days from other years. This estimates thermal activity within ±15 days, not official ignition, containment or extinction dates. A regional envelope can contain several fires. Available AOI archive: 2001-04-23–2026-08-26.

- Estimated dry biomass consumed: **36,074.121 tonnes**, using 0.368 kg/MJ. [1]
- PM2.5 emission estimate unavailable: measured annual fuel support is incomplete.
- Assumed-factor CO2 emissions: **56,997.111 tonnes**, using 1,580 g/kg dry biomass.

These are model and factor-based scenario estimates, not measured emissions, ambient PM2.5 concentrations or burned hectares. Emission factors vary with fuel and combustion. ### Sensor & Statistical Verification

Active sensors: **Aqua, SNPP, Terra**; reconstructed days: **0**. Reconstruction enabled: **yes**. Selected polygon area: **830.542 km²**. [4] [6]

Circular mean of annual peak months: **4.94** (1=January, 12=December; 15 years). Post/pre-2012 raw counts per recorded cube day: **35.627×**. This descriptive ratio includes coverage and real variability; it is not an isolated sensor effect. Industrial candidates in the full AOI history: **0 cells**, **0 cube detection counts**; these are screening counts, not distinct facilities or fires. [10]

This is a statistical thermal-activity classification, not confirmation of vegetation fuel or an identified wildfire. MODIS and VIIRS differ in resolution and sensitivity; calibrated FRE is used instead of comparing raw counts as fire totals. The episode profile sums within-cell sensor fusion times exact cell areas, with industrial sources excluded. Dashboard density is that sum divided by the selected polygon area. Unknown days remain unfilled; only explicitly evidenced gaps permit reconstruction. This is a sampled model-derived energy proxy, not a continuous physical measurement. H3 cell centers define the selection, not an administrative boundary or mapped fire perimeter. [2] [3] [5]

**59,515.938 GJ** of mapped, observation-based energy proxy for **2022-08-15 to 2022-08-28** in **Bejís, Castellón — Iberian pilot**. [6]

Regional temporal estimate: **59,515.938 GJ**, over **14 days**, including **0 reconstructed days**. Both fuse available sensors within each cell and use exact H3 areas; the map contains observations only. [6]

Derived dry biomass: **21,901.865 tonnes**, using 0.368 kg/MJ. This is a calibrated one-hour integration proxy from sparse satellite samples, not continuously measured heat release, burned area or measured emissions. [1]

Observed cell footprint: **377.314 km²**; selected polygon: **830.542 km²**. Available through **2022-08-28**. Industrial sources excluded.

The archive records 1,723 satellite detections and an integrated energy of 59,515.938 GJ between August 15 and August 28, 2022, representing thermal activity consistent with active vegetation burning rather than verified individual fires [5] [6]. Detections concentrate between August 15 and August 19, reaching a peak on August 17 with 807 detections and 25,032.485 GJ [5] [6]. 

Because spatial detections have not been matched against an official incident perimeter, any named wildfire in the surrounding Iberian area serves strictly as broader regional context. Individual grid-cell observations cannot be affirmatively attributed to a specific incident's perimeter, nor do they represent continuous tracking, as polar-orbiting satellites measure instantaneous power only during discrete overpasses [5] [K1] [K10].
